notes: §1985:VI.6.10.2 is DISPLAY, one or more identifier-1 or literal-1 operands, then the UPON mnemonic-name-1 phrase and the "[ WITH <u>NO</u> <u>ADVANCING</u> ]" phrase, each optional and in that order; it prints no scope terminator, no exception phrase and no positioning phrase. The grammar rule displayStatement requires one operand, repeats it, then takes displayUpon and displayNoAdvancing once each in the printed order (WITH optional), followed by the 2023 additions, and 1985 reaches three refusals of those: VersionConformancePass.VisitDisplayStatement refuses END-DISPLAY below COBOL-2002 (COBOL0816), and AcceptDisplayBinder.BindDisplay refuses at every edition a positioning phrase (ScreenFormatOf, COBOL1707, the declined screen format) and an exception phrase on a device DISPLAY (DeviceFormatPhrase, COBOL2269). The witness displays an identifier, a literal and the identifier again in one statement. Probed further at --std 85: operands separated by commas, figurative constants (ZERO, SPACE, QUOTE, HIGH-VALUE, LOW-VALUES, ALL literal), numeric literals, a subscripted and a reference-modified identifier, UPON with WITH NO ADVANCING, NO ADVANCING alone and UPON alone all compile and run; END-DISPLAY, ON EXCEPTION, NOT ON EXCEPTION, AT LINE and LINE positioning, NO ADVANCING before UPON, a second UPON phrase, WITH ADVANCING, and DISPLAY with no operand are each refused.

next.reason: 1985: "DISPLAY {identifier-1|literal-1} … [ UPON mnemonic-name-1 ] [ WITH NO ADVANCING ]"; 2023: "DISPLAY {identifier-1|literal-1} … [ UPON mnemonic-name-1 ] [ WITH NO ADVANCING ] [ END-DISPLAY ]". 2023 Format 1 keeps the operands, UPON and WITH NO ADVANCING, but adds an optional END-DISPLAY. 2023 accepts DISPLAY statements that the 1985 format refuses.
